courses.title: CERN Open Data

courses.note: Use CERN’s own education examples. Do not republish datasets here.

courses.title: Physics, philosophy, history — course slides

courses.note: Free Substack post. Slide files stay on his host.

courses.note: Public OCW. Later editions of the textbook are not hosted.

courses.note: Creator: Grant Sanderson. Link-out only.

courses.title: Introduction to Neuroscience
courses.whyAdvanced: A public introductory neuroscience course. Old term, real syllabus. Not a wellness podcast.
courses.note: Seated on the data-to-ML path because that is the existing life-science-adjacent parent. Not a clinical credential.

courses.title: Allen Brain Map
courses.whyAdvanced: Open brain-wide data. The lab seat next to 9.01.
courses.note: Allen Institute for Brain Science. Do not mirror the datasets.

courses.title: Demystifying active inference
courses.whyAdvanced: Friston and coauthors’ open review of active inference: perception and action as one variational principle. The bridge from neuroscience to the ML sittings.
courses.note: Authors include Noor Sajid, Philip J. Ball, Karl J. Friston. Read the arXiv version, not a paywalled reprint.

courses.title: Huberman Lab
courses.whyAdvanced: Andrew Huberman’s public neuroscience conversations. Seated as outreach, under 9.01, not above it. Not a medical protocol and not a credential.
courses.note: Podcast and show notes. Do not treat episode claims as a syllabus.

courses.title: A True and Faithful Relation (Casaubon / Dee)
courses.whyAdvanced: The printed relation of Dee’s records. Read it as a document. This track is source-critical digital Hermetica, not a ritual school.
courses.note: Discussed on r/occult as a table source. Seat the Archive scan, not a modern how-to.

courses.title: Thrice-Greatest Hermes (Mead translation)
courses.level: Primary text in an old translation
courses.whyAdvanced: An open English Hermetica. Copenhaver’s critical edition is the scholarly standard and is not hosted. Mead is the free text, with that limitation labeled.
courses.note: Not a ritual manual. Encoding a table is a programming exercise; encoding is not mysticism.

courses.title: European Society for the Study of Western Esotericism
courses.whyAdvanced: The academic map for esotericism as history. Use it to tell a source from a costume.
courses.note: Society site. Journal articles may sit behind a publisher; we do not copy them.

courses.title: Hermetica: a community list of texts and fragments
courses.whyAdvanced: A public attempt to list religio-philosophical Hermetica, including contested fragments. A shelf card, not a canon we certify.
courses.note: Community list. Litwa’s Hermetica II is named there and is a copyrighted edition — library, not this site.

courses.title: TinyML and Efficient AI Computing
courses.whyAdvanced: Song Han's public EfficientML course: compression, quantization, NAS, on-device LLM. Link-out to Han Lab site — not an OCW mirror.
courses.note: Public syllabus + live.efficientml.ai stream. Enrollment/Canvas are MIT-only; we link the public course page only.
Paid tier exists; free edition linked
courses.title: The Pragmatic Engineer
courses.whyAdvanced: Gergely Orosz's long-running newsletter on how engineering organizations actually work — hiring, org design, incident culture, system design, and shifts in the tech industry. Useful reading for thinking like a senior engineer rather than just coding like one.

courses.note: Paid tier exists; free edition linked
courses.title: ByteByteGo
courses.whyAdvanced: Alex Xu and Sahn Lam's newsletter explains large-scale systems with visuals and plain language — caching, queues, consistency, database internals. Directly trains the vocabulary and trade-off reasoning used in system design interviews and architecture reviews.

courses.title: SRE Weekly
courses.whyAdvanced: A long-running curated roundup devoted to keeping sites and services available and fast — incident writeups, monitoring, SLOs, and reliability culture. Steady input for building an SRE mindset around measurement and postmortems.

courses.title: Platform Engineering Weekly
courses.whyAdvanced: Curated coverage of platform engineering — internal developer platforms, paved paths, and the practices that let product teams ship without owning infrastructure. Pairs with the platform/SRE path for understanding the platform-team role.

courses.title: Refactoring
courses.whyAdvanced: Luca Rossi's newsletter on growing as an engineer — code craft, design judgment, and career strategy. Complements the hands-on labs with the professional habits that distinguish hired engineers from hobbyists.

courses.title: Engineer's Codex
courses.whyAdvanced: Essays on leveling up as a software engineer — technical depth plus the strategy of navigating engineering careers. Good companion reading for the career-change narrative the platform is built around.

courses.title: Engineering At Scale
courses.whyAdvanced: Explains databases, system design, and architecture with plain-language breakdowns, alongside engineering career guidance. A steady source of architecture intuition for backend and platform topics.

courses.title: Latent Space
courses.whyAdvanced: The AI engineer community's publication — practical coverage of building with LLMs, agents, evals, and production ML systems. The right on-ramp for the AI engineering track without academic overhead.

courses.title: Coding Challenges
courses.whyAdvanced: John Crickett's newsletter of hands-on programming challenges and problem-solving walkthroughs. Builds the coding-interview muscle with regular practice rather than passive reading.

courses.title: ByteByteGo
courses.whyAdvanced: The video arm of the ByteByteGo newsletter — short, visual explainers on how systems like Kafka, CDNs, and payment flows work, plus full system-design interview walkthroughs from the book's authors.

courses.title: Gaurav Sen
courses.whyAdvanced: Gaurav Sen builds system design from first principles — load balancing, sharding, consistency — with whiteboard-style depth, plus algorithms and LLM content. Strong for learners who want the why before the what.

courses.title: Hussein Nasser
courses.whyAdvanced: Deep backend dives — TCP, HTTP internals, Postgres locks, proxies, kernel-level networking — explained through real scenarios. The channel that takes learners past surface-level system design into how the machine actually behaves.

courses.title: XRPL.org Developer Documentation
courses.whyAdvanced: The canonical reference for how the XRP Ledger works: accounts, transactions, the native DEX, and consensus. Engineers learn XRPL by reading protocol behavior here, not by guessing from price charts.

courses.title: XRP Faucets — Testnet and Devnet Funds
courses.whyAdvanced: Real test environments require funded test accounts; the faucet is the sanctioned way to get test XRP for devnet/testnet builds. Every XRPL integration exercise starts here.

courses.title: xrpl.js — JavaScript/TypeScript API for the XRP Ledger
courses.whyAdvanced: The standard client library for building XRPL payment and tokenization apps in JavaScript/TypeScript. Reading its source teaches how transactions are constructed, signed, and submitted to a ledger.

courses.title: xrpl-py — Python API for the XRP Ledger
courses.whyAdvanced: The Python counterpart to xrpl.js, maintained by the XRPL Foundation. Engineers who work in Python can build wallets, payment flows, and ledger automation directly against the XRPL APIs.

courses.title: XLS-20: Non-Fungible Tokens on the XRP Ledger
courses.whyAdvanced: XLS-20 defines native NFTs on XRPL — no smart contracts required. Studying the standard shows how a ledger can add token primitives at protocol level instead of via contract code.

courses.title: XLS-30: Automated Market Makers on the XRP Ledger
courses.whyAdvanced: XLS-30 added native AMM pools to the XRPL's built-in decentralized exchange. The spec is a compact case study in automated market-maker math and on-ledger liquidity design.

courses.title: Ethereum Developer Documentation
courses.whyAdvanced: The official starting point for Ethereum development: accounts, gas, the EVM, and the contract development stack. Engineers use it as the reference map before touching any contract code.

courses.title: Solidity Documentation
courses.whyAdvanced: The authoritative language reference for Solidity. Security bugs in smart contracts usually trace to misunderstood semantics; this is where engineers verify what the compiler actually does.

courses.title: OpenZeppelin Contracts Documentation
courses.whyAdvanced: OpenZeppelin's audited contract library is the industry baseline for tokens, access control, and upgradeable proxies. Learning its patterns is how engineers avoid rewriting — and re-breaking — standard primitives.

courses.title: CryptoZombies — Interactive Solidity Tutorial
courses.whyAdvanced: A hands-on, browser-based Solidity course that teaches by writing and deploying contracts lesson by lesson. Best used as the interactive companion to the official Solidity docs.

courses.title: Bitcoin Developer Documentation
courses.whyAdvanced: The technical reference for Bitcoin Core: transactions, scripts, P2P networking, and running infrastructure. Required reading for anyone operating nodes or reasoning about Bitcoin's security model.

courses.title: Learn Me a Bitcoin
courses.whyAdvanced: A precise, ground-up technical explainer of Bitcoin: hashing, signatures, scripts, and blocks, each with worked examples. Builds the mental model that makes protocol documentation readable.

courses.title: The Daily Gwei
courses.whyAdvanced: A daily Ethereum-focused newsletter covering protocol upgrades, L2 developments, and ecosystem shifts. Engineers use it to stay current on the network their contracts deploy to.

courses.title: Bankless
courses.whyAdvanced: A long-running crypto newsletter covering DeFi mechanics, token economics, and protocol governance. Useful for engineers who need to understand the economic systems their code participates in.

courses.title: Building on the XRP Ledger — Training Part 1
courses.whyAdvanced: A hands-on XRPL developer training covering accounts, payments, tokenization, stablecoins, and AMMs on the ledger. Practical walkthrough of the concepts the docs describe in text.

courses.title: Learn Blockchain, Solidity, and Full Stack Web3 Development with JavaScript – 32-Hour Course
courses.whyAdvanced: A full course by Patrick Collins via freeCodeCamp covering Solidity, Hardhat, ethers.js, DeFi, NFTs, and contract security. The closing security and auditing section is the most valuable part for engineers.

courses.title: Oracle Java SE Documentation
courses.whyAdvanced: The canonical reference for every Java SE release: API specs, language guides, and tool docs straight from the platform owner. When a Stack Overflow answer and the docs disagree, the docs win.

courses.title: The Java Tutorials
courses.whyAdvanced: Oracle's official trail-based tutorials covering language basics through generics, collections, and concurrency. The shortest credible path from zero to writing real Java.

courses.note: Exam registration is paid; the page lists objectives and recommended prep training.
courses.title: Java SE 17 Developer (Exam 1Z0-829)
courses.whyAdvanced: The official OCP Java SE 17 exam page with the full objective list: streams, modules, concurrency, JDBC, and localization. Studying to its objectives is one of the most structured ways to close gaps in core Java.

courses.title: Inside Java
courses.whyAdvanced: Written by the Oracle engineers who build the JDK: release deep-dives, GC behavior changes, and design rationale. Essential reading for anyone who tunes or operates JVMs in production.

courses.note: Requires a free Oracle account to take quizzes.
courses.title: Free Java Quizzes | Oracle Dev Gym
courses.whyAdvanced: Weekly multiple-choice quizzes on reading real Java code, from beginner to expert level, authored by professional Java developers. The fastest way to find what you don't actually know.

courses.title: Oracle Learning Explorer: Free Training & Accreditation
courses.whyAdvanced: Oracle's free entry-level training and accreditation across OCI, databases, and applications, with hands-on labs. A no-cost on-ramp into the Oracle ecosystem before committing to paid certs.

courses.note: Always Free services carry usage limits; the trial credit expires after 30 days.
courses.title: Oracle Cloud Free Tier
courses.whyAdvanced: Always Free OCI services including Ampere compute, Autonomous Database, and object storage. Lets you stand up real cloud infrastructure for labs and portfolio projects without a bill.

courses.title: Oracle Database Free
courses.whyAdvanced: The free edition of Oracle Database (23ai) for development and learning, including AI Vector Search and JSON Relational Duality. Run the real enterprise database locally instead of only reading about it.

courses.title: Oracle Database 23ai Documentation
courses.whyAdvanced: The complete 23ai documentation library: SQL language reference, PL/SQL, security (including SQL Firewall), and new AI features. The reference every Oracle DBA and backend engineer eventually lives in.

courses.title: JVM Weekly
courses.whyAdvanced: A Substack newsletter by Artur Skowronski that dissects JDK releases with real terminal output: JEPs, GC defaults, and crypto changes. Keeps your JVM knowledge current without reading every mailing list.

courses.title: Java Full Course for Beginners (Programming with Mosh)
courses.whyAdvanced: A single 2.5-hour video taking beginners from installing Java through types, control flow, and clean coding. A dense, well-structured first exposure before tackling the official tutorials.

courses.title: Java tutorial for beginners (Bro Code)
courses.whyAdvanced: A long-running beginner Java playlist with short, exercise-style videos covering everything from variables to OOP. Good for repetition-driven practice alongside a main course.

courses.title: Java Tutorial For Beginners (Telusko)
courses.whyAdvanced: Telusko's Java series goes beyond syntax into the ecosystem topics backend interviews probe. A solid second source once the fundamentals are in place.

courses.title: awesome-java
courses.whyAdvanced: A heavily starred curated list of Java frameworks, libraries, and tools across every category. The fastest way to survey the ecosystem and pick battle-tested dependencies.

courses.title: Introduction to Linux (LFS101)
courses.whyAdvanced: Builds the command-line fluency everything downstream assumes: filesystem, permissions, processes, package management. Short on time, long on payoff before touching certs or cloud.

courses.title: Linux System Administration Essentials (LFS207)
courses.whyAdvanced: The practical companion to the LFCS exam: user and package management, filesystems, networking, and kernel interaction across Debian/Ubuntu and RHEL families. Turns Linux familiarity into administrable systems.

courses.title: Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator (LFCS)
courses.whyAdvanced: A performance-based sysadmin exam that tests doing, not memorizing: storage, networking, services, and troubleshooting on live systems. Pairs directly with LFS207 and mirrors RHCSA-adjacent skills employers screen for.

courses.title: Kubernetes Fundamentals (LFS258)
courses.whyAdvanced: The official on-ramp to the CKA: cluster architecture, workloads, networking, and storage taught hands-on. Worth taking before any exam-prep video so the terminology actually sticks.

courses.title: Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)
courses.whyAdvanced: The performance-based K8s admin credential: install, configure, troubleshoot, and secure production-grade clusters from a live terminal. The single most legible signal for platform and SRE-adjacent roles.

courses.title: Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD)
courses.whyAdvanced: The developer-facing counterpart to CKA: application design, configuration, observability, and lifecycle on Kubernetes. Useful once cluster basics are solid and the goal shifts to shipping on the platform.

courses.title: Introduction to Cloud Infrastructure: Describe Cloud Concepts
courses.whyAdvanced: Microsoft's own AZ-900-aligned path covering cloud models, shared responsibility, and service types. Short and free; gives Azure vocabulary needed before the administrator and developer tracks.

courses.title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate
courses.whyAdvanced: The official AZ-104 hub: study guide, free practice assessment, and linked learning content for identity, governance, storage, compute, and networking on Azure. The natural next step after AZ-900 for ops-minded engineers.

courses.title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Developer Associate
courses.whyAdvanced: The official AZ-204 hub for building and deploying on Azure: compute solutions, storage, security, and monitoring with Microsoft's own modules and practice assessment. Fits the dev track of a cloud career.

courses.title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Fundamentals
courses.whyAdvanced: The official DP-900 hub covering relational and non-relational data, analytics, and data workloads on Azure. Lightweight entry point that rounds out cloud fluency beyond compute and networking.

courses.title: Microsoft Certified: Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals
courses.whyAdvanced: The official SC-900 hub: Microsoft Entra ID, Zero Trust, compliance, and threat protection concepts. Security vocabulary that transfers to every cloud and every interview.

courses.note: Representative issue of the weekly 'IT News You Can Use' newsletter; covers Linux, DevOps, storage, AI, and security topics.
courses.title: IT News You Can Use (Data Connectors)
courses.whyAdvanced: A working-engineer newsletter digest that regularly surfaces Linux, DevOps, storage, and security stories with practitioner context. Cheap ambient awareness of what the industry is actually arguing about.

courses.note: Linux Foundation grant-funded full course (~2 hours) on the freeCodeCamp channel.
courses.title: Kubernetes Course – Certified Kubernetes Administrator Exam Preparation (2026 Update)
courses.whyAdvanced: A full freeCodeCamp CKA walkthrough from cluster bootstrapping with kubeadm to troubleshooting, produced with a Linux Foundation grant. Best paired with LFS258: watch, then drill every command yourself.

courses.title: AZ-900: The Complete Microsoft Azure Fundamentals Course
courses.whyAdvanced: Every AZ-900 objective taught in one three-hour sitting with animated diagrams and Azure CLI demos, linking out to Microsoft's official study guide and practice assessment. A solid visual complement to the Learn path.
